positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described witnessing a traumatic incident where someone was seriously hurt. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reported recurrent thoughts and flashbacks triggered by sounds or environments. Criterion B2 (intense physical/psychological reactions): MET — patient mentioned experiencing racing heart and feeling shaky when reminded of the event. Criterion C1 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient stated they try to avoid thinking about the event and engage in grounding techniques. Criterion C2 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient reported avoiding places and conversations that remind them of the trauma. Criterion D1 (negative alterations in mood): MET — patient expressed feelings of negativity about themselves and the world. Criterion D2 (blame): MET — patient described moments of self-blame regarding the trauma. Criterion D3 (negative feelings): MET — patient reported feelings of fear and guilt. Criterion D4 (diminished interest): MET — patient indicated a reduced interest in activities they previously enjoyed. Criterion D5 (detachment): MET — patient described feeling disconnected from others. Criterion D6 (inability to experience positive feelings): MET — patient noted challenges in experiencing good feelings. Criterion E1 (irritability): MET — patient reported increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion E2 (recklessness): MET — patient mentioned engaging in risky behaviors like driving faster. Criterion E3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient described feeling more anxious and on guard. Criterion E4 (startle response): MET — patient reported being more easily startled. Criterion E5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient noted difficulty concentrating. Criterion E6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient described disrupted sleep. Criterion F (duration): MET — symptoms have persisted for over a year. Criterion G (functional impairment): MET — patient reported significant distress and interference with daily functioning. Criterion H (exclusion): MET — patient denied substance use or medical conditions contributing to symptoms. Total: 14 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
